items.title: George Shearing interviewed by Joe Williams, New York City, New York, March 8, 1996
items.q: You know, a philosophy that Duke had, I always found very interesting.

ctx.x: I think he wanted to be like that, you know, with Tom Whaley, who also was a wonderful musician. You’d hear Duke tell him what he was going to do, and that was an experience, to hear him tell Tom Whaley, “well here, do our thing here and you know, B natural thing here, and you know, run this thing down, you know what we do, do our thing here.” And he’d say, “Oh I know what you mean.” Anybody else — Jimmie Jones is there, and Strayhorn was there, and said what the heck are they talking about?

You know, a philosophy that Duke had, I always found very interesting. You’d get a new man in the band and he would very rarely ask that man to play like so-and-so and so-and- so. He says “I don’t want that. I want that man to contribute what he has to contribute.”

There you go. That was Ellington, that was Basie. Basie had more people come through there, and it was whatever you had to contribute. That was what I was telling Leslie a while ago. I said Basie chose “Alright, O.K., You Win.” Everything else in that repertoire I chose to do. I’d have to fight him to be able to do it somewhat, because he’d say “oh you don’t need that, just do what you’re doing.”
